buildingBriefs.cover: The outbuildings break the yard into cover and blind corners: the woodshed and the well hide a body, and a walk to the privy at night leaves the house's walls behind.
buildingBriefs.facade: The house's long rendered face to the road, a trodden path down one side to the yard, and in some plots a blockwork garage beside the house with its opening to the road.

bedroom.purpose: Sleeping, at the back of the house, away from the road.

kitchen.purpose: Cooking and eating at the back of the house.

living_room.purpose: The house's front room across the road side, warmed by a wood stove.

toilet.purpose: The household's toilet: the privy at the far end of the yard, or the WC of a modernised house.

woodshed.purpose: The stove's firewood, stacked dry under a roof across the yard from the back door.

references: Balkan and Greek village plots of the 1970s and 1980s: the house at the road, a walled or fenced yard behind it with a well, a woodshed, a hen house and the privy at the far end.
Finnish and Swedish country houses of the same decades: the house by the road, a woodshed and outhouse across the yard, and a separate garage beside the house once the family had a car.

buildingBriefs.cover: Few, small windows give a defender narrow views of the road and yard; the open plot round the house means no approach is hidden for long, and the back door is the weak point.
buildingBriefs.facade: A plain, symmetrical street face: a door with a small canopy, regular window pairs, a plinth course and a coping at the roof line. The back is busier, with the kitchen door, a lean-to and a coal or log store.

bedroom.purpose: Sleeping; upstairs when the cottage has a second storey.

kitchen.purpose: Cooking and eating; the back door to the yard opens from it.

living_room.purpose: The front room, facing the road.

references: Post-war rural brick cottages: one or one-and-a-half storeys, a central or offset front door, two windows each side.
Small farm workers' houses of the 1950s to 1970s, rendered block over a concrete plinth, with a lean-to at the back.
Roadside smallholdings: the house close to the road, a yard and outbuildings behind it.

buildingBriefs.cover: The walls stop shots and the windows are few and small; the flat roof behind its parapet is a firing step for whoever gets up there. The porch has no door to close, so the back is the only door that holds.
buildingBriefs.facade: A long, low rendered face to the road on a stone plinth course: a centred porch under the projecting slab, a window either side, and the parapet coping as one clean line along the top. Some houses clad the entrance bay in timber boards.

bedroom.purpose: Sleeping, at the back, away from the road.

kitchen.purpose: Cooking and eating at the back; the back door to the yard opens from it.

living_room.purpose: The front room across the road side, entered straight from the porch and warmed by a wood stove.

references: Yugoslav rural houses of the 1970s and 1980s: owner-built rendered blockwork cubes under a flat concrete slab, a parapet round the roof and the slab edge left projecting as a plain cornice.
Greek and Cypriot village houses of the same decades: reinforced-concrete frame and flat roof behind a low parapet, rendered walls, a shallow concrete band at the roof line.
Finnish and Swedish flat-roofed detached houses of the 1960s and 1970s: low, white-rendered, with dark-stained timber boarding at the entrance and a broad fascia.

kitchen.purpose: Cooking at the back; the back door to the yard opens from it.

living_room.purpose: The front room across the road side, entered straight from the porch and warmed by a wood stove.

wc.purpose: A small WC off the front room, plumbed in when the house was modernised.

references: Yugoslav rural houses of the 1970s and 1980s: owner-built rendered blockwork cubes under a flat concrete slab, a parapet round the roof and the slab edge left projecting as a plain cornice.
Greek and Cypriot village houses of the same decades: reinforced-concrete frame and flat roof behind a low parapet, rendered walls, a shallow concrete band at the roof line.
Finnish and Swedish flat-roofed detached houses of the 1960s and 1970s: low, white-rendered, with dark-stained timber boarding at the entrance and a broad fascia.
Village houses modernised in the 1970s and 1980s: a WC and basin partitioned off the back rooms once a water main or a septic tank reached the house, the old privy left in the yard or pulled down.
